getTaskStatus() -- a separate call from use()/send(). Corrected both
docstrings and the co-located TS guide doc to point there instead of at a
field that doesn't exist.

subscription receives apaevt_flow enter/leave events for every lane write

matching the prior analysis.

forward to the monitor stream) is built entirely inside
`if self._pipelineTraceLevel:` -- there's no unconditional flow event, only
a conditional one. LogEventStream (packages/client-python/src/rocketride/
log_stream.py, client.log.open_event_stream(...)) is the existing public SDK
surface for that stream, and its get_traces()/get_trace(trace_id) are the
direct match for "every lane write and invoke call" the original docstring
promised -- more precise than the componentStats/slowestDocs aggregate
542716f8 (this issue's first fix) pointed at, which is a real but coarser
derivative of the same underlying events.

Updated both SDK docstrings and the guide doc to lead with
LogEventStream.get_traces()/get_trace(), keeping the componentStats mention
as the secondary (aggregate analytics) answer.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment by CodeRabbit for review status -->

My blocker is closed — `docs/agents/ROCKETRIDE_python_API.md:456` and `ROCKETRIDE_typescript_API.md:438` no longer promise a `_trace` field, so the highest-traffic surface for this mistake is fixed.

The four commits since also went well past what I asked for, adding a lot of new, specific, falsifiable detail. I checked all of it against source rather than reading it for plausibility, and almost everything is exactly right — with one clause that repeats the same class of error this PR exists to fix.

## Verified correct

Every LogEventStream claim in the new prose is a faithful condensation of the implementation:

- **`get_traces(n)` = "open + the `n` most-recently-closed trace summaries, `n` must be <= 50"** — `log_stream.py:321-341` returns `{'open': ..., 'closed': closed[-n:]}` and raises `ValueError` when `n > _MAX_TRACES`, with `_MAX_TRACES = 50` at `:88`.
- **"reads state as of the session's position and returns nothing before a seek"** — `get_traces` reads `self.position()`, which is `_base_pos` (initialised to `0.0` at `:184`) until a seek sets it. `_ensure_covering_segment(0.0)` finds no span starting at or before the epoch, so a pre-seek call really does fold nothing. That is a non-obvious behaviour and it is worth documenting.
- **`get_trace(trace_id)` "is position-independent and needs no prior seek"** — it never touches `position()`; it refreshes the timeline and resolves by seq. Matches its own docstring.
- **The identity contract** — "`trace_id` is the trace's begin-event continuum seq (its permanent identity), not the flow event's `body.id`, which is a reused pipe slot" is a near-verbatim condensation of `log_stream.py:346-352`: *"a trace is identified by its BEGIN event's continuum seq — the only key that is unique forever. The flow events' `body.id` is a pipe SLOT, reused across requests, and cannot name a trace."* This is the single most useful sentence added in this PR.
- **`seek('live')`** — `:246` takes "epoch seconds, or 'live' to pin to now".

## Blocking: "both stay empty at 'none'" is not true when the pipeline invokes tools

The new clause appears in all five files, and it conflates *omitting the parameter* with *passing the string `'none'`*. Those take different branches.

The engine half of the claim is right, and I confirmed it:

- `config.hpp:180` — `PIPELINE_TRACE_LEVEL pipelineTraceLevel = PIPELINE_TRACE_LEVEL::NONE;`
- `endpoint.config.cpp:281-286` — only `"metadata"`, `"summary"`, `"full"` are recognised; the literal `"none"` and an absent value both leave it at `NONE`.
- Every emission site gates on `traceLevel >= PIPELINE_TRACE_LEVEL::METADATA` (`binder.cpp:118,148,169`, `filter.callbacks.target.cpp:111,126`), so at `NONE` no lane-write or invoke traces are emitted.

The SDK half is where it breaks:

- `task_engine.py:340` — `self._pipelineTraceLevel = _args.get('pipelineTraceLevel', None)`. Omitted gives `None`; `'none'` gives the **non-empty string** `'none'`.
- `task_engine.py:1551` — the gate is `if self._pipelineTraceLevel:`, plain truthiness. `None` is falsy; `'none'` is **truthy**.
- The code comment three lines above says why that matters: *"synthetic tool-call traces arrive regardless of trace level."* Confirmed — `data_conn.py:844` `_emit_tool_trace` is called from seven sites (`:949, :981, :990, :1008, :1010, :1030`), none of them gated on trace level, and it routes through the same `monitorOther('DBG', ...)` channel the C++ debugger uses, so `transport_stdio.py:861` turns it into an `apaevt_trace` that lands in that handler.

So:

| `pipelineTraceLevel` | C++ traces | tool-call traces | `if self._pipelineTraceLevel:` | analytics |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| omitted (`None`) | none | emitted | falsy — skipped | **empty** |
| `'none'` | none | emitted | **truthy — runs** | **populated from tool calls** |
| `'metadata'` / `'summary'` / `'full'` | emitted | emitted | truthy | populated |

A pipeline with tool invocations, run with `pipelineTraceLevel='none'`, builds `apaevt_flow` events and accumulates `componentStats` — the docs now say it will not. The in-code comment at `:1566` calls the falsy path "no traces, honest empties", which is precisely the state you only get by omitting the parameter.

Narrow and mild in consequence — some extra tool-call analytics, nothing broken. But this PR's entire deliverable is that the documentation matches the code, and I held the last round to that standard, so I am holding this clause to it too.

Suggested wording, inline. The short version is to stop asserting equivalence: say `'none'` is the engine's default level and emits no lane-write or invoke traces, and tell people to **omit** the parameter when they want nothing recorded at all.

Worth a separate issue for the code side — normalising `'none'` to `None` at `task_engine.py:340`, or making `:1551` compare against `'none'` explicitly, would make the docs' natural reading true and is the fix I would actually want. Out of scope for a docstring PR.

## Not blocking

The rest of the diff is good. Scoping this to documentation rather than implementing `_trace` for real is the right call for a Low-severity doc bug, and saying so in the description is better than silently narrowing it.

Fix the one clause across the five files and I will approve.
